title: finding(plugin-timeline): a gantt-variant timeline reads a date-only end as the START of that day, so an inclusive end (Jan 1 to Jan 31) draws one day short of its column, and a same-day task draws zero-width
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site, class (a). `reach:` a named producer, measured. `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/plugin-timeline/gantt-style-timeline.json` writes inclusive date-only ends: API Design `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-31`, QA Phase `2024-03-01` to `2024-04-30`. The objectui#11079 dev laid the rendered gantt out in Chromium (1200 px, not committed). The API Design bar's right edge sits at x 442.406, while the Feb header begins at x 450.734: one day short of its month column.

Reader: triage first (grade and route), then the seat that dispatches it. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`) at the landing of PR objectui#11109 (objectui#11079), from the dev report's `out_of_scope_findings` (`5891523619`). That PR's contract review (`5891777944`, ③) confirmed it at the head as a pre-existing read-rule question. The base's equal-width columns masked the gap by coincidence (30 / 120 = 1/4). ⛔ Not graded here.

## What happens

`packages/plugin-timeline/src/renderer.tsx` reads every gantt date through `readGanttDate`, the objectui#10866 slice-3 rule. A date-only string is that day's local midnight, which is the start of the day.
- **An inclusive end draws one day short.** A task authored `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-31` means "through January 31". Its bar ends at the start of Jan 31, one day before the February column begins.
- **A same-day task draws zero-width.** A task whose date-only `startDate` equals its `endDate` has zero length, so its bar is invisible on any plan. After PR objectui#11109 that includes a one-day plan: the objectui#6750 pin now reads `left: 0%; width: 0%`, where the old guard drew full width.

`TimelineGanttItemBar.endDate` in `packages/types/src/data-display.ts` declares neither an inclusive nor an exclusive reading. The catalog producer authors inclusive ends.

## Direction (for triage, not a ruling)

This is a read-rule decision for the gantt variant: is a date-only `endDate` inclusive (drawn through the end of the named day) or exclusive?
- **Inclusive** matches the producer and ordinary project-plan authoring. It is a one-place change at the end read: the end of a date-only day is the next day's start. A `datetime` end keeps its instant, per objectui#10866's binding reading.
- A same-day task then draws one day wide. If a zero-length item should instead read as a milestone marker, that is a separate, product-shaped question.
- Compare `plugin-gantt`'s own convention for a date-only end before choosing, so the two gantt surfaces agree.

Pins: the catalog producer's bars end exactly at their month columns' ends; a same-day date-only task has a visible width; a `datetime` end is unchanged, under Los Angeles and Shanghai (the objectui#10866 zone-pin driver).

## Dedupe

The 1100 most recently updated objectui issues and PRs, open and closed (down to #2231), were listed via REST and grepped locally:
- `inclusive`: 3 hits, none about a gantt end: objectui#10750 (flow decision), and PR objectui#10957 and PR objectui#10994 (month clamping, DST days).
- `milestone`, `zero-width`, `one day short`, `endDate inclusive`, `exclusive end`: 0 hits each.
- `gantt-style-timeline`: 2 hits, PR objectui#10901 and PR objectui#10957 (the date-only zone reads). Neither decides the end's inclusivity.
- `TimelineGanttItemBar`: 1 hit, PR objectui#10822 (declaring the item's shape).
- Absent control `zzqq_never_written_token_4242`: 0 hits.

No card covers this.
